original_question: Inside the unit 3-sphere S^3 subset E^4, are the only finite type surfaces the minimal surfaces, the standard 2-spheres, and the products of two plane circles?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Conjecture 2: "Minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres and products of two plane circles are the only finite type surfaces in S^3 ⊂ E^4." ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's actual target almost word-for-word: it uses the same ambient space S^3 ⊂ E^4, asks about finite type surfaces, and lists exactly the same three families named in Conjecture 2. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
missing_details: The paper's notion of finite type is with respect to the Euclidean position vector of an isometric immersion x:M→E^4: one requires a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk with Δxi=λi xi for the Laplace operator Δ on M. Your draft leaves this definition implicit. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

Section 2.1 sets the ambient framework as an isometric immersion of a connected Riemannian manifold; for a stand-alone question, it is better to say 'let x:M^2→S^3⊂E^4 be an isometric immersion of a connected surface.' ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

The nearby context makes precise what 'products of two plane circles' means in S^3: the 2-type examples are S^1(a)×S^1(b) with a^2+b^2=1, and in the genuinely 2-type case a≠b. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

For stand-alone readability, the phrase 'standard 2-spheres' should be unpacked explicitly, since the paper states it without definition. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

The conjecture is global and is not restricted to compact surfaces; that should remain clear in the rewrite. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency data are relevant here; the only missing operator-level datum is the Laplacian appearing in the finite-type definition. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
refined_question: Let x:M^2→S^3⊂E^4 be an isometric immersion of a connected surface into the unit 3-sphere, viewed as a submanifold of Euclidean 4-space. Assume that M is of finite type in the sense of Chen, namely that its Euclidean position vector admits a finite spectral decomposition x=c+x1+...+xk with Δxi=λi xi for the Laplace operator Δ on M. Must M be one of the following and only these: (i) a minimal surface in S^3, (ii) a standard round 2-sphere in S^3, or (iii) a product S^1(a)×S^1(b) of two plane circles in S^3, with a^2+b^2=1 (and, in the nonminimal 2-type case, a≠b)? ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
justification: The draft clearly points to Section 4.1's Conjecture 2 rather than to the neighboring classification problems, because the paper first records the exact classification of 2-type surfaces in S^3 as products S^1(a)×S^1(b) with a≠b and a^2+b^2=1, then states the broader conjecture that the only finite type surfaces in S^3⊂E^4 are minimal surfaces, standard 2-spheres, and products of two plane circles. The finite-type terminology used in that conjecture is defined earlier in Section 2.1 through the spectral decomposition of the Euclidean position vector. ([journals.math.tku.edu.tw](https://journals.math.tku.edu.tw/index.php/TKJM/article/viewFile/1564/873))
